message.content:
The `.*` regexes are commented out. Let me look at the active regex patterns more carefully. Let me look at the `fortran` regex `!\^[^Cc\ \t].*$`:

The regex `\^[^Cc\ \t].*$` requires at least one character (the `[^Cc\ \t]` part), so it can't match empty.

Let me look at the `SAM` regex `=^([^\t]+\t){2}\\*|[^*=]*\t`:
- `=^([^\t]+\t){2}` - two tab-separated fields
- `\\*` - literal `*` (in regex: `\*`)
- `|` - OR
- `[^*=]*\t` - zero or more non-*, non-= characters followed by tab

The second alternative `[^*=]*\t` can match empty if followed by a tab. But it requires at least a tab.

Wait, I need to think about this differently. The glibc bug is about regexec returning 0 but not initializing pmatch. This happens when the regex matches an empty string. Let me look at what regex patterns can match empty strings.

A regex like `^` (start of line) matches an empty string at the start of any line. A regex like `$` matches an empty string at the end of any line. A regex like `x*` matches an empty string anywhere.

Let me look for regex patterns in the magic database that can match empty strings:
